Once upon a time there was a Hare who loved to run.
Zoom!
Round and round the meadow he went, faster than anyone in the whole wood.
Squirrel, Hedgehog and Frog sat on a log and watched.
I'm the fastest animal in the world!
said Hare.
Nobody can ever beat me!
Just then the Tortoise came along the path.
She walked very slowly, one little step at a time.
Slow and steady, step by step,
said Tortoise.
Hello, Tortoise!
Look how fast I am!
I could run to the old oak tree and back before you get to the end of this path!
Shall we have a race, then?
said Tortoise with a smile.
To the old oak tree on the hill?
A race? With me?
Yes, please!
This will be easy!
A race! A race!
said Squirrel, and she jumped up and down on the log.
Along came wise old Owl.
I'll be the judge!
said Owl, and he drew a line across the path with his stick.
The Hare and the Tortoise stood side by side on the line.
Squirrel, Hedgehog and Frog clapped and cheered.
Ready... steady... GO!
said Owl.
Off went the Hare like the wind.
Off went the Tortoise too, one little step at a time, and her three friends walked along beside her to cheer her on.
The Hare ran so fast that soon he was far, far ahead.
He stopped and looked back.
The Tortoise and her friends were tiny dots, far down the path.
This is too easy!
I've got time for a little nap.
The Hare lay down in the cool shade of a big tree.
He shut his eyes, and soon he was fast asleep.
Snore...
snore...
The Tortoise kept on walking.
Past the pond and round the bend she went, one little step at a time.
Go, Tortoise, go!
said Frog, and she did a happy hop.
Ribbit!
Soon they came to the big tree where the Hare lay fast asleep.
Wake up, Hare!
We're still racing!
Her friends called too.
But the Hare just rolled over and went on snoring.
Up, up, up the hill went the Tortoise.
Owl had flown on ahead, and he was waiting by the finish line under the old oak tree.
said Squirrel, and she waved her bushy tail.
You're nearly there!
Down below, the Hare woke up with a great big yawn.
He looked up the hill, and he saw the Tortoise near the top!
Uh-oh! The race!
The Hare ran as fast as he could.
But the Tortoise took one more little step, and she was over the finish line.
The Tortoise wins!
Hooray! Hooray! Hooray!
said Hedgehog, and he clapped his little paws.
The Hare puffed up to the old oak tree.
He was out of breath, but he smiled and held out his paw.
Well done, Tortoise!
You won, fair and square.
I'm sorry I boasted.
Thank you, Hare,
You're still the fastest runner I know!
That evening everyone sat together under the old oak tree and watched the sun go down.
Slow and steady wins the race,
said Hare with a smile.
Tomorrow let's go for a walk together, Tortoise.
And from that day on, the Hare and the Tortoise were the best of friends.
